children: Australian stocks look set to follow U.S. equities lower after military strikes around the Strait of Hormuz caused a spike in oil futures and bond yields. ASX futures are down by 0.9% ahead of Wednesday's session, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 is on course for a third consecutive decline. The benchmark index has lost 0.4% so far this week amid growing expectations that the country's central bank will resume interest-rate rises later this month. Shares including in Origin Energy, Seek, PLS and Downer EDI will trade ex-dividend Wednesday. In the U.S., the DJIA fell 0.8%, the S&P 500 shed 0.7%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 1%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
